sections.title: Quick Answer
sections.content: The best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone is **QuranWall**. It is built for one job: putting an ayah on your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or a translation. Below, it is compared with five other Quran widget apps, read from their US App Store listings on 18 November 2026. QuranWall is our app, so it is ranked first here; this is the honest case.

sections.text: Most lists of Islamic apps point you to a reader or a prayer-times app and call it done. But if your real goal is to *see* the Quran without opening anything, the apps to compare are the ones that put a verse on the Lock Screen. This guide ranks the **best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone** against five real Quran widget apps, then covers the reading, memorizing and prayer-time apps worth keeping beside it. For a wider ranking of Muslim apps, see our [best Muslim app for iPhone](/blog/best-muslim-app-for-iphone-2026) guide.

sections.label: phone checks a day
sections.description: Americans say they check their phones about 186 times a day, per Reviews.org's 2026 survey of about 1,000 US adults (self-reported). A verse on the lock screen turns those glances into small reminders.

sections.text: What makes a great Islamic lock screen app
Not every app labelled Islamic belongs on your lock screen. The **best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone** clears a short, strict bar:

items: **Lives on the lock screen.** A real widget or wallpaper, not a notification you swipe away.
**Easy to keep fresh.** Changing the verse takes a few taps, and a widget that rotates on a schedule keeps it from going stale.
**Built for the surface.** Designed to sit right under the clock, not a reading-app screenshot.
**No ads.** Nothing competing with the verse for your attention.

QuranWall vs other Quran widget apps, side by side

Many apps on the US App Store put a Quran verse on the iPhone Lock Screen, and these six are the ones this guide compares. They differ mostly in what they bundle around the verse: QuranWall keeps to the ayah, while Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas, Muslim: Quran Quotes and Quran Widgets by Noor add prayer times and more. Each row comes from that app's own listing.

| Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas | Widgets that show a verse, a dua or an Islamic quote; live and static wallpapers inside the app | The Quran with its translation (languages not named) | One app for verse widgets, prayer times, qibla and dhikr |

| Quran Widgets by Noor | Ayah, dua and dhikr widgets for the Lock Screen, Home Screen and StandBy | Arabic with English, several translations | A reflection feed with widgets, prayer times and a tasbih counter |

Read both tables as a snapshot, not a verdict: every fact comes from the app's own App Store listing, and listings change with each update. Where a listing does not name its translation languages, the table says so instead of guessing. Two things stand out. QuranWall's listing is young and has two ratings so far, while Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas has thousands, so that gap in social proof is real. And the minimum iOS varies a lot: QuranWall installs on iOS 15.0 (its Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widget need iOS 16), only Muslim: Quran Quotes goes lower (iOS 13.0), and Quran Quotes Widget needs iOS 26.0.
The best Islamic lock screen apps for iPhone, ranked

QuranWall ranks first because it does one job, the verse on the Lock Screen, without bundling prayer tools around it. The other five follow by how closely their listing matches that job, and each one is the better choice for a particular reader, named in its heading.
1. QuranWall — built for the Lock Screen (our pick)

**QuranWall** wins because it is built around one job: putting a Quran ayah on the surface you already see all day. It sets the ayah as your Lock Screen wallpaper and Home Screen widget, in Uthmani Arabic or in a translation, in your choice of 10 languages. You choose the background, font and colours — a preset or your own photo — and you can search all 114 surahs by surah, ayah or keyword. There are no ads, and the Quran text works offline.

To change the wallpaper, pick a new ayah and tap **Make It Mine**; Apple's Shortcuts app applies it. The widget is the part that can change by itself: turn on auto-rotate and it shows a new ayah daily, every 8 hours or hourly.

New to it? Start with the [iPhone lock-screen setup guide](/blog/quran-verse-iphone-lock-screen), or pair it with a [Quiet Time Focus mode](/blog/quran-focus-mode-iphone) so your Quran lock screen appears around your prayer times.
2. Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas — best all-in-one widget app

With thousands of US ratings, this is the most-rated app in this comparison. Its listing describes Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets that show a verse, a dua or an Islamic quote, live and static wallpapers, and a long list of extras: prayer and iftar times (also as widgets), qibla, a mosque finder, a dhikr counter and zakat tracking. Pick it if you want one app for all of that. The trade-off is focus: the verse is one feature among many, and it needs iOS 17.6.
3. Ayat: Quran Widget & Quotes — best for a rotating widget with notes

Ayat's listing centres on widgets: small, medium and large Home Screen widgets, plus Lock Screen widgets on supported devices, showing random verses, one you choose, or ayat from your collections, changing anywhere from hourly to daily. It adds English meanings, downloadable translations and personal notes on the verses your widget showed. Per the listing, its Arabic text follows the Hafs narration from the King Fahd Glorious Quran Printing Complex. It needs iOS 18.0.
4. Muslim: Quran Quotes — best for reminders plus prayer tools

Its listing puts Quran quotes and hadith reminders on the Lock Screen and pairs them with prayer times and adhan, qibla, a fasting tracker and a Ramadan calendar, plus a Quran reader. It suits someone who wants Lock Screen reminders and prayer tools in the same place, and it is the only app here that installs on iOS 13.0.
5. Quran Quotes Widget — best for a wallpaper that changes daily

Quran Quotes Widget is the one app here whose listing says it can refresh the Lock Screen wallpaper daily with a new image, next to Home and Lock Screen widgets in English, Arabic or both. It also lets you pick favourite surahs and use photos from your library. The catch is the requirement: iOS 26.0, so older iPhones cannot install it.
6. Quran Widgets by Noor — best for a feed plus widgets

Noor's listing pairs a scrollable feed of ayat and duas with widgets for the Lock Screen, Home Screen and StandBy that can show an ayah, dhikr, the next prayer or the Hijri date. It also has prayer times, a qibla compass, a tasbih counter and a question-and-answer companion. Choose it if you want widgets and a daily reflection feed in one app.
Apps worth keeping for other jobs

Muslim Pro, Quran.com, Quran Majeed, Tarteel and Athan are not Lock Screen apps, but each is good at its own job, and many readers keep one of them next to a Lock Screen verse app. Here is what each is for, so you can tell which gap it fills.
Muslim Pro — best for prayer times and qibla

Muslim Pro is the long-standing all-in-one: accurate prayer times, qibla direction, adhan, and a Quran reader. If you want a single app for the daily prayer schedule, it's a strong choice. What it isn't is a lock-screen app. The Quran stays inside it, one tap away rather than already in front of you.
Quran.com and Quran Majeed — best for reading and tafsir

For sitting down to read, Quran.com (from the Quran Foundation) and Quran Majeed are excellent: clean Arabic, several translations, tafsir, and audio. They are reading tools, though. They are where you go to study, not what greets you when you lift your phone.
Tarteel — best for memorization
Tarteel uses AI to follow your recitation and support hifz, catching slips as you memorize. For that narrow, important job it's genuinely useful. It does nothing for your lock screen.
Athan by IslamicFinder — best for adhan reminders

Athan is built around prayer-time notifications and the adhan. If reminders to pray are your gap, it fills it well. But a prayer alert isn't a verse you read; it's a notification you act on and dismiss. If remembrance is your gap rather than prayer times, see the [best dhikr app for iPhone](/blog/best-dhikr-app-for-iphone).

sections.content: Notice the pattern. Muslim Pro is for prayer times. Quran.com and Tarteel are for reading and memorizing. Athan is for the adhan. QuranWall and the five widget apps above are for the surface you check all day: the Lock Screen. Among those, choose by what you want beside the verse: read-along audio per ayah and an optional romanized line (QuranWall), your own notes (Ayat), or a full prayer toolkit (Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas, Muslim: Quran Quotes, Noor).

sections.text: Which one should you pick?

Pick by what else you want on your phone. If you want the verse and nothing competing with it, in your own background, font and colours, choose **QuranWall**. If you want verse widgets and prayer times in one app and value a large base of ratings, choose Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas. If you want notes on the verses your widget shows and your iPhone runs iOS 18, choose Ayat. If your iPhone is older (iOS 13 or 14), Muslim: Quran Quotes still installs. If you run iOS 26 and want the wallpaper itself to change daily, Quran Quotes Widget's listing says it does that.
Where this gets hard

You could skip the apps and just save a verse image as your wallpaper. Two things break it. First, a reading-app screenshot isn't designed for the lock screen, so the text lands under the clock, the margins are off, and it looks like a screenshot because it is one. Second, the habit dies by week two. Changing your wallpaper by hand is a small chore you'll quietly stop doing.

**QuranWall** removes both problems. It is designed for the lock-screen surface, so you are not screenshotting, cropping or exporting images into your Camera Roll. Changing the ayah takes a few taps inside QuranWall, and the widget can show a new ayah every day if you turn on auto-rotate.
How to set it up

items: Open it and choose your translation language, background, font and colours.

Pick an ayah and tap **Make It Mine** to set it as your Lock Screen wallpaper (the first time, the app walks you through adding its shortcut in Apple's Shortcuts app), then add the QuranWall widget to your Home Screen.
Optional: add a lock-screen widget from the lock-screen editor, or, on iOS 16 or later, link that Lock Screen to a Focus (touch and hold the Lock Screen, then tap Focus).
Your ayah now meets you every time you check your phone. To change it, pick another and tap Make It Mine again.

sections.content: QuranWall installs on iOS 15.0 or later, but its Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widget need iOS 16 or later (on iOS 15 you get the Home Screen widget). Apple added Lock Screen widgets and per-Focus lock screens in iOS 16, so for those parts of this guide, update in Settings > General > Software Update first if your iPhone is older.

sections.text: Frequently asked questions
Does it work on every iPhone?

QuranWall installs on iOS 15.0 or later, but its Lock Screen wallpaper and Lock Screen widget need iOS 16 or later, and Lock Screen widgets and per-Focus lock screens arrived in iOS 16, so most steps in this guide need iOS 16 or later; on iOS 15 you get the Home Screen widget.
Is QuranWall the only Quran lock screen app?

No. Many Quran widget apps are on the App Store, and five are compared above: Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas, Ayat: Quran Widget & Quotes, Muslim: Quran Quotes, Quran Quotes Widget and Quran Widgets by Noor. QuranWall ranks first here because it keeps the Lock Screen for the verse alone, and because it is our app; read the listings and decide for yourself.
Can a Quran app change my Lock Screen wallpaper by itself?

Quran Quotes Widget's listing says it can refresh the wallpaper daily, on iOS 26. QuranWall's wallpaper changes when you pick an ayah and tap Make It Mine. For a verse that changes on a schedule, use the QuranWall widget with auto-rotate turned on: daily, every 8 hours or hourly.
What is a good Muslim Pro alternative for the Lock Screen?

Muslim Pro is a prayer-times app, so the alternative depends on the job. For a Quran verse on the Lock Screen, QuranWall is our pick. If you also want prayer times in your widgets, the listings for Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas and Muslim: Quran Quotes name both.
Which Quran widget app has the most ratings?

Of the six apps compared here, Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas had the most US ratings on 18 November 2026, followed by Muslim: Quran Quotes. QuranWall's listing has two so far. Ratings measure popularity, not whether an app fits your Lock Screen, so weigh them with the tables above.

sections.title: The short version
sections.content: For reading, choose Quran.com. For prayer times, Muslim Pro. For memorizing, Tarteel. For verse widgets plus prayer tools, Quran Widgets: Verses & Duas. But for the **best Islamic lock screen app for iPhone** (an ayah on the surface you already check, with nothing else competing for it), QuranWall is our pick.
